diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume the oracle noise along the iterates satisfies the uniform conditional second-moment bound
Under Algorithm \ref{alg:main_psa} with the recursion $v_{t+1} = \Pihat\Bigl((1-\alpha_t)v_t + \alpha_t\,\widehat T(v_t)\Bigr)$ and $\alpha_t=\alpha/(t+1)$

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma's stated hypotheses are only the uniform conditional second-moment bound \E[||T̂(v_t)−(r+Pv_t)||_∞^2|F_t]≤σ² and the stepsize α_t=α/(t+1), with no constraint on α. Its written proof needs two conditions that are never assumed: (i) conditional unbiasedness \E[ξ_{t+1}|F_t]=0, asserted 'by the oracle condition' but not implied by a second-moment bound, and used to cancel the martingale cross term in the second-moment expansion; and (ii) 0≤α_t≤1, needed for the triangle-inequality step \|(1−α_t)e_t+α_tΠPe_t\|_q ≤ (1−α_t)‖e_t‖_q+α_tγ‖e_t‖_q, which is unjustified when α>1 (the coefficient 1−α_t is then negative). The lemma also invokes \|Π̂x\|_∞≤2‖x\|_∞ without stating the simplex property of b̂ it rests on. As written, the stated conclusion sup_t \E‖v_t−v*‖_q²≤C_stab is not established by the given argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the lemma's hypotheses the two standard conditions its proof actually uses — conditional unbiasedness \E[Π̂T(v_t)|F_t]=Π̂(r+Pv_t) (satisfied by the generative oracle of Algorithm alg:main_psa) and 0<α_t≤1 (e.g. t_0=1 with α≤1, as in Lemma lem:projSA_stability_template) — and cite Lemma lem:b_simplex for the ℓ∞ bound on Π̂; the written proof then goes through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:optionB_stability's stability and bounded-iterates guarantees are unsupported as written. The lemma is not cited by any downstream labelled result, so no other result is invalidated.
issues.title: Stability lemma's proof relies on unstated oracle unbiasedness and stepsize range
issues.why_classification: A local, routine repair (adding two standard conditions that the paper's own oracle and sibling lemma already satisfy) completes the argument; conclusion, rate, and advertised scope are unchanged, so this is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Assume the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:projSA_stability_template} hold and that
\(\alpha_t=\alpha/(t+t_0)\) with \(t_0\ge \max\{\alpha,1\}\).
Assume the SA stepsizes are $\alpha_t=\alpha/(t+t_0)$ with $t_0\ge \alpha$ and $a=\alpha(1-\widehat\gamma)>1/2$.

issues.failure_explanation: Corollary cor:optionB_rate assumes only t_0 ≥ α and a=α(1−γ̂)>1/2, then proves itself by the one-line invocation 'Apply Theorem thm:projSA_rate_template'. The cited theorem, however, requires t_0 ≥ max{α,1}; when α<1 and t_0∈[α,1) — admissible under the corollary's stated hypotheses (e.g. α=0.9, γ̂ small enough that a>1/2) — the invocation violates the theorem's hypothesis. On that slice the theorem's key potential-function step, bounding Σ(t+t_0)^{2a−2} by ∫_{t_0−1}^{T+t_0} x^{2a−2}dx = ((T+t_0)^{2a−1}−(t_0−1)^{2a−1})/(2a−1), is ill-defined since (t_0−1)<0 is raised to the non-integer exponent 2a−1∈(0,1). The corollary's stated bound is therefore not established by its proof for admissible parameters.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State t_0 ≥ max{α,1} (the condition already carried by the cited Theorem thm:projSA_rate_template) in Corollaries cor:optionB_rate and cor:end_to_end_v; this imposes no cost since t_0 is a free parameter, and every rate and query-complexity conclusion survives verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The O(T^{-1/2}) rate to v̂* and the end-to-end query-complexity guarantee (Corollaries cor:optionB_rate and cor:end_to_end_v, and their informal counterparts Lemma/thm:main_sa_rate and cor:main_end_to_end_v) are unproven for the admissible parameter regime t_0∈[α,1); the guarantees themselves remain plausible and are restored by carrying the missing condition.
issues.title: SA rate corollary invokes the rate theorem outside its stepsize hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A one-word strengthening of the corollaries' hypotheses (t_0 ≥ 1) makes the cited theorem apply verbatim; the rate, constants, and end-to-end guarantee all survive, so the repair is a routine local hypothesis fix with no mathematical loss.
